backup.production_rule: Two live functions are replaced and one is added. Neither body was retyped: a script cut each from its applied migration, asserted the cut hashes to the live md5(prosrc) read on 2026-09-24 (run_system_verifier_v1 12b080bfff25b908f20bf4ae3813af9e, apply_verifier_run_v1 acc043e2048f9d88e0109ce8d7200f36), then applied exact one-hit replacements. The forward checks assert the resulting bodies' md5. No table, column or policy is altered. Rows change only through the new auto-resolution 3 (a confirmed reservation's dates from its confirmed calendar row; nights is generated, never money) and the answer RPC (recon_status). The backup is taken as the LAST act before the apply (D-210).

rollback.safe_until: always. Nothing depends on telegram_answer_calendar_block_v1 except telegram-expense's cb:block tap, which then writes the RPC error on the card.

steps.name: run_compensating_script
steps.action: apply supabase/rollbacks/20260925_verifier_v7.sql with run-sql-on-host.sh. It restores both functions to their pre-release bodies (asserts md5 12b080bf... and acc043e2...), drops telegram_answer_calendar_block_v1 and closes open V7/V7b/V13 findings, which the old scope arrays would never resolve. Corrected reservation dates stay: they are the Airbnb calendar's dates.

feature_flags.name: v7_fires_only_after_calendar_sync_v15
feature_flags.required_state: No calendar row carries linked_reservation_id before calendar-sync v15 (waves 7d223a0) is deployed, so V7 and V7b are silent until the first sync after that deploy. The SQL goes first so apply_verifier_run_v1 knows V7/V7b/V13 before anything raises them.

compatibility.rehearsal: Rehearsed 2026-09-24T13:19Z on a disposable restore of production backup cascade-supabase-20260924T131354Z (taken for the rehearsal, newer than B120's release; prefix cascade-migration-rehearsal-cce8bdc996c9, 0 leftovers). 102 public tables and 123 ledger rows before, 102 after; the migration applied, 1 of 1; forward checks 7/7 against real data; pgTAP verifier_v7_dates_mismatch.sql 31/31, verifier_triage_and_opening_amounts.sql 22/22, system_verifier_phase1.sql 32/32, health_checks_core_v10.sql 25/27 - the two failures are its grant assertions on health_checks_core_v1 and run_health_checks_service_v1, which a --no-acl restore cannot carry; both read true on production at 13:20Z. The FIRST rehearsal (prefix f33891783374, same backup) failed the new suite: airbnb_reservations.nights is a generated column, so auto-resolution 3 would have raised in production on its first V7; fixed in 5dd0bf3 (dates only) and re-rehearsed.
compatibility.evidence: The system-verifier live before waves 7d223a0 renders an unknown check with its stored title and 'open the dashboard', so the SQL applied before the deploy cannot produce a broken card; nothing raises V7/V7b/V13 before that deploy anyway. pgTAP verifier_v7_dates_mismatch.sql (31 assertions) and verifier_triage_and_opening_amounts.sql (its 72-hour red assertion inverted for D-232).

stop_conditions: any forward verification query returns anything other than its expected value
either md5 check fails - that is a mistyped body, not a flaky assertion
the restore point is older than one hour
restore_point or verified_at is still empty
the rehearsal has not run the pgTAP suites green on this commit
